clue.text: Throw punches, taking time over risky jab?

indicators.note: the boxing word takes in the other letters, holding them in its middle

parts.note: to throw punches is to box
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A boxer, punching away, takes a moment to consider whether a dangerous jab is worth the risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw punches' and 'jab' suggest a boxing match, but the jab here is an injection.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic injections of botulinum toxin carry some danger, so the treatment is playfully called a risky shot in the face.

clue.text: Profligate, playing awful set

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spendthrift gambler is losing money on a dreadful set of tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate person squanders money recklessly, which is the core sense of being extravagant.

clue.text: State of British administered East India

parts.note: to run something is to administer it
E is the compass abbreviation for east
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A historical note about a territory governed by the British East India Company.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the East India Company, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a sovereign sultanate on Borneo, a nation in its own right.

clue.text: Bill, the magistrate

definitions.meaning: British slang for a magistrate or judge

explanation.surface: Bill turns out to be the local magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the horny mouth of a bird, and old British slang for a judge on the bench.

clue.text: Desperate character, German, in peril

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman from the British children's comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A desperate German is in mortal danger.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a burly cowboy in The Dandy, a long-running British children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is exposure to harm, a near synonym for risk or jeopardy.

clue.text: During battle, trap a noble mounted general

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the letters climb upwards, so they read backwards
the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A general climbs on his horse in the middle of a battle, setting a trap for an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' hides the letters ETRAPANOB in 'battle, trap a noble'; 'mounted' turns them upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the French military commander and emperor, the most famous general in history.

clue.text: Recycling of clearer water vital to its survival

definitions.text: Recycling of clearer water vital to its survival

indicators.note: recycling processes material again into a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An environmental message: keeping seawater clean is essential for the survival of a marine habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycling' rearranges OF CLEARER, while the whole clue describes the habitat that depends on clean water.
explanation.definitionFit: Reef-building corals are very sensitive to pollution and need clean, clear seawater to stay alive.

clue.text: Lord's seeing Boycott getting to grips with run out

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it, so the first word encloses the others

parts.note: to boycott something is to ban it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is short for out, as on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: At Lord's cricket ground, Geoffrey Boycott is struggling against a run-out.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground and Geoffrey Boycott a famous Yorkshire batsman, but here a lord is a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is the lowest rank of the British peerage, addressed as Lord.

clue.text: The last thing from Nevil Shute: novel made into film

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement
the final letter of the following word is all that is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A literary note about the final novel by the author Nevil Shute being adapted for the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Nevil Shute was a novelist, so 'novel' seems part of the picture, but it is the anagram signal; Sleuth was in fact a play by Anthony Shaffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleuth, a stage thriller, was filmed in 1972 with Laurence Olivier and Michael Caine, and again in 2007.

clue.text: Mass location maybe where holy person is garlanded with blessing

indicators.note: a garland wreathes around something, so the blessing word surrounds the saint

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A church where a saint's statue is hung with flowers, as if a Catholic Mass were being held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service, but it is short for Massachusetts, the US state whose capital this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is the capital city of Massachusetts, so it is one place in that state, shown by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Spilling milk crossing rough road regularly wasted well over two pounds

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stretch across the others, holding them inside
spilt milk is scattered, so its letters are jumbled
every other letter of the phrase is thrown away, leaving alternate ones

explanation.surface: Milk spills as a cart bumps along a rutted track, wasting a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spilling' turns MILK into KILM, and 'crossing' sets it round the kept letters; 'well over two pounds' is a weight, not a quantity of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric kilo equals about 2.2 imperial pounds, comfortably more than two.

clue.text: Testify, condemning 'Mr FIFA'

indicators.note: to condemn something is to wreck its standing, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A witness gives evidence against the head of world football's governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: FIFA is world football's governing body, often accused of corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to declare under oath, and to affirm is the secular form of that solemn declaration.

clue.text: Servant seen with with nothing below the waist in priest's residence

parts.note: a man is an old word for a manservant

indicators.note: only the top half of the following word is kept, as if cut off at the waist

explanation.surface: A half-dressed servant is spotted in the vicar's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The doubled 'with' is a typo in the printed clue; the top half of SEEN is SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a minister, especially in the Scottish Presbyterian church.

clue.text: United spin row creating mayhem

parts.note: U is a standard abbreviation for United, as in football team names
PR, public relations, is the business of putting spin on things
you row with an oar

explanation.surface: A football club's media spin over a dispute causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, fitting the mayhem, but it is the rowing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a noisy commotion, close to chaos or pandemonium.

clue.text: Being cautious, made it out of the group stage?

definitions.meaning: a ... statement is guarded and hedged with reservations

definitions.text: made it out of the group stage?
definitions.meaning: a team that progresses from the group stage of a tournament has earned its place in the next round

explanation.surface: A football team played it safe and reached the knockout rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is restricted or hedged; the other is having earned a place in the next round of a competition.

clue.text: Launch hotel web address

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a URL is the address of a web page

explanation.surface: A hotel unveils its new website address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch' suggests a website going live, but it means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch an object can mean to throw or fling it hard.

clue.text: Table Mountain, Switzerland?

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether Table Mountain might be found in Switzerland rather than South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Table Mountain is in Cape Town; here it splits into the definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench is a work table, as in a carpenter's or laboratory workbench.

clue.text: Be mostly against dam' hard worker?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of the word is used, the end being cut off

parts.note: averse means opposed or against

explanation.surface: Someone told to be largely opposed to a hard worker who is cursed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam'' reads as the curse 'damn', but points to the animal that builds dams.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal famously builds dams and is proverbially industrious, as in the idiom about being as busy as one.

clue.text: Washington Times: The Measure of Power

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Washington
T is time, so times in the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline, as if the Washington Times ran a feature on political power.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like a newspaper and a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of power is named after James Watt, the Scottish steam-engine engineer.

clue.text: Having grappled with the others, went first

parts.note: the rest means the others
to lead is to go first, past tense led

explanation.surface: A wrestler took on the rest of the field and came out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple with an opponent, so the past tense matches this phrase.

clue.text: Godfather actor not in old American material

indicators.note: not means these letters are left out of the actor's name

parts.note: Al Pacino starred as Michael Corleone in The Godfather

explanation.surface: An actor from The Godfather is absent from some old American fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is a cloth woven from the soft wool of the South American animal of that name.

clue.text: Leisurely mover better going topless

indicators.note: the top letter of the word, its first in a down entry, is taken off

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: A relaxed stroller is doing better after shedding their top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like a comparative, but it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strolls at a gentle pace is a slow walker, someone who saunters.

clue.text: Knocking back beer, Cruz possibly is very happy

indicators.note: knocking back means drinking, and back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
Ted Cruz is a US senator, one example of a person called Cruz

explanation.surface: A politician downing a pint is in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' suggests drinking, but it sends ALE backwards. Ted Cruz is a Texas senator.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means overjoyed or thrilled.

clue.text: Gaza, leaderless, getting a visit from Bush

indicators.note: the answer drops in on the words, sitting inside them as a visitor

explanation.surface: A leaderless Gaza receives a visit from President Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' reads as the US president, but it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: An azalea is a flowering shrub of the rhododendron family.

clue.text: Patient chap embracing a cold patriarch

indicators.note: the outer word hugs the other letters inside it

parts.note: Job is the biblical figure proverbial for patience
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A patient man hugs an old leader suffering from a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob is one of the three founding fathers of Israel in Genesis, alongside Abraham and Isaac.

clue.text: Rotten luck, getting one that turns

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
a break is a stroke of luck, as in a lucky break

explanation.surface: Someone has bad luck and receives something that goes sour.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an off-break is a ball spun by the bowler to turn from the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket delivery is spun so that it deviates after pitching, so it turns.

clue.text: Swiss-born artist moving first piece of luggage to bottom part of ship

indicators.note: this word says a letter is shifted from its place in the artist's name
in a down entry, the bottom is the end, where the letter is placed

parts.note: Paul Klee was a painter born in Switzerland

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: An artist relocates luggage to the hold of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of KLEE, matching luggage's first letter, moves to the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The keel is the structural spine running along the bottom of a ship's hull.

clue.text: Errant husband leaving resting place for Senior Service?

indicators.note: the husband leaves, so his letter is taken out

parts.note: Senior Service was a British cigarette brand, and a cigarette is rested in an ashtray

explanation.surface: An unfaithful husband walks out of his naval career.
explanation.walkthrough: Senior Service is a nickname for the Royal Navy, but here it is a British cigarette brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering from the proper path, so off course.

clue.text: Philosopher's male haircare product?

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
gel is used for styling hair

explanation.surface: A question of which hair gel a philosopher uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a German idealist thinker of the early 19th century.

clue.text: Romeo: build deep love, and build again

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to build here is to put the letters together in a new shape

explanation.surface: Romeo hopes to rebuild a deep love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'build' appears twice: first as the anagram signal, then in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To redevelop an area is to rebuild or renovate it.
